analysis.title: US Treasury Market Daily: There and back again
key_insights: Front-end yields spiked 15bp higher in the morning after a hot September CPI, and money markets priced close to 50% odds of an October hike, but the move retraced in the afternoon, likely on Governor Bowman's comments in Bangkok that she didn't feel any urgency for further action.

JPM sees the next Fed hike in December, describing the Fed as data dependent but not data point dependent. Chair Warsh's comments tomorrow evening are the key near-term event and the last major input before the blackout period.

JPM sees value emerging at current yields because OIS forwards have priced a full unwind of last year's insurance cuts. It prefers to stay patient before adding outright duration, citing few catalysts to push yields lower and positioning that is still a headwind.

The Treasury Client Survey showed the sharpest weekly decline in outright longs this year, leaving the share of longs at its lowest since mid-August. The survey index still leans long overall, unlike prior hiking cycles, so a wholesale reduction in those overweights could push yields higher.

Treasury's dealer questionnaire for the November refunding is due out at noon ET. There is heavy speculation that Treasury could float cutting or discontinuing 20-year bond issuance. JPM does not think this would be prudent.

JPM's argument against cutting 20-year issuance: a significant funding gap is opening in FY27 and beyond, and the 20-year raises $168bn annually. The TBAC minutes cite a median dealer forecast of a $1.45 trillion privately-held funding shortfall for FY2027-28.
JPM's fair-value model for the 20-year, with an R-squared of 96.6%, shows long-end yields in line with fundamentals. In fall 2023 they traded more than 50bp above model value.

JPM cannot rule out the question being asked, because Treasury more than doubled long-end buyback sizes two weeks after the August refunding and Secretary Bessent wants lower long-term yields. It expects any benefit absent fiscal consolidation to be short-lived, citing the UK DMO and Japan MoF experience.

Treasury could also ask about market functioning, since liquidity has deteriorated in the yield rise but only reverses a small part of the structural improvement. It could also ask about repo volumes, which are down 10% from their peak earlier this year.

September CPI headline rose 0.65% m/m with energy up 5.2% m/m and food flat. Core CPI rose 0.33% m/m against 0.2% consensus, with core goods at +0.25% (the highest m/m in a year) and core services at +0.37%.
Supercore CPI (core services ex housing) rose 0.42% m/m, the highest since April. JPM says this wage-driven category should give the Committee pause before the October FOMC.

OER rose 0.35% m/m and rent 0.25%. Excluding an April spike tied to the government shutdown, this is the largest OER increase in 18 months. The Midwest rose 0.72%, and JPM argues it was not payback for a small rise when the panel was last sampled.
JPM's estimates imply a 0.31% m/m core PCE print, lifting the y/y rate from 3.0% to 3.1%.

Headline CPI exceeded swap market pricing by more than 7bp, the largest upside surprise since March 2024. This lifts November TIPS carry (5-, 10- and 30-year at 11bp, 6bp and 3bp) and shifts the inflation data surprise backdrop to upside risks. JPM had taken profits on its 2Yx3Y zero coupon inflation swap narrowers on Friday.

Treasury is expected to announce mid-month supply tomorrow at 11am: $13bn reopened 20-year bonds and $26bn new issue 5-year TIPS, both unchanged in size. JPM expects the 5-year TIPS roll to open at -5.75bp (range -6.8 to -4.8bp).

Technicals: the 10-year staged a bullish intraday reversal after retesting the 5.29-5.32% support layer, following a selloff that produced the most oversold conditions in years on some indicators. The bullish view strengthens if yields break below the 5.15% recent low.

trade_ideas.description: Stay patient before adding outright Treasury duration positions
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning is still a headwind and few catalysts are ahead to drive yields materially lower.
trade_ideas.risk: A wholesale reduction in long overweights could drive yields higher.

risk_factors: A wholesale reduction in the survey's long overweights could drive yields higher.
Few first-tier data releases between now and the October FOMC leave few catalysts to push yields lower.
Chair Warsh's comments tomorrow evening could shift Fed hike pricing.
Treasury could use the refunding questionnaire to float cutting or discontinuing 20-year issuance.
Upside inflation surprises: supercore, shelter and core goods firmness point to more persistent price pressures.

Portfolios do not appear braced for a full Fed tightening cycle, because the survey index remains long-leaning unlike in prior hiking cycles.

tension_points.bull_case: Treasury cutting or ending 20-year issuance could lower long-term yields temporarily, and the August buyback increase suggests discomfort with yield levels given Secretary Bessent's stated goal.
tension_points.bear_case: A significant funding gap opens in FY27 and beyond, the 20-year raises $168bn annually, and long-end yields are in line with fundamentals. UK and Japan experience suggests any benefit would not last.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of a dislocation in long-end yields versus the fair-value model, like the fall 2023 gap of more than 50bp above model value.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot CPI with firm supercore and shelter raises the odds of an October hike, and money markets briefly priced above 50%.
tension_points.bear_case: Governor Bowman, President Williams and Vice Chair Jefferson stress no urgency, pointing to a more patient Committee. JPM sees the next hike in December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Chair Warsh's comments tomorrow evening, the final major input before the Fed blackout period.
